correctness.rationale: Reconstructible analytic proof: the two distinct cosine-phase progressions have spacing 2π/K and, over four sine-monotonicity branches, give 4K/π+O(1) scalar inverses uniformly in target/phase. The actual printed map has amplitudes K_y=H and K_x=πH, giving 16H²/π=256/(πb²). Branchwise bounded-variation grid quadrature yields O(1/K) normalized Wasserstein-1 error and triangular conditioning yields product law O(b). Chain-rule determinant factorization shows critical ancestors O(1/b). Explicit finite checker directly verifies map identities in 95 configurations and 70,328 points; finite tests are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The precise order and leading constant of target ambiguity are natural structural invariants of the very 2D map proposed as a high-complexity cosine chaos generator, and are not supplied by forward plots. The limiting spatial density is nonuniform, vanishes at sine turning points, and is independent of coupling and target; the O(b) transport rate and asymptotic regular fraction characterize the geometry and distribution of the many inverse sheets. The claimed facts address a well-defined gap without relying on speculative claims about forward chaos or cryptographic safety.
